name: Benton & Sons
old_description: Custom fabricated steel parts and components, structural steel fabrications, steel machine bases and more. Specializes in large component steel fabrication.
about:
Benton & Sons Fabrication operates from Pikeville, North Carolina, about 60 miles southeast of Raleigh. Founded in 1983 by the Benton family, the business remains family‑owned and operated, with three generations having worked in the shop. Owner Ben Benton Jr. now leads a company that has grown into one of the largest plate‑rolling, brake‑press‑forming, and machinery‑assembly facilities in the southeastern U.S.

The 100,000‑sq‑ft facility includes multiple bays, large overhead doors, and overhead cranes for oversized work. Core capabilities cover heavy steel plate fabrication, stainless steel sheet metal fabrication, plate rolling, brake‑press forming, laser cutting, water‑jet cutting, punching, shearing, welding, and custom machinery assembly. Key equipment includes a 1,000‑ton × 24‑ft CNC Cincinnati brake press, a TRUMPF 6,000‑watt TruLaser 5060, and a Mitsubishi 6030XL laser cutter — each noted as rare in the region. Output ranges from custom steel parts, structural fabrications, and machine bases to stainless enclosures, commercial kitchen equipment, pharmaceutical and lab equipment, and metal yard art.

Customers span the Southeast and Mid‑Atlantic, including Maryland, Virginia, the Carolinas, and Georgia. Served industries include food processing, commercial kitchens, pharmaceutical plants, shipbuilding, nuclear facilities, transportation, beverage bottling, and fine chemicals. Access to I‑95, I‑40, rail, and East Coast ports enables worldwide shipment of large assemblies.

The company stresses quick turnaround, on‑time/on‑budget delivery, and an experienced workforce. During the 2008‑2009 recession, ownership commissioned a large dinosaur sculpture to keep workers employed and hone fabrication skills, underscoring a commitment to workforce stability and continuous improvement.
